title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Non-Timber Forest Products"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Non-timber forest products cover what forests yield other than wood. The account values them per
hectare of forest people can actually reach. The base year is 2019 and the price convention
recorded in `es_config.csv` is `value per accessible hectare`. No share is taken out for human
inputs (λ = 1), as the write-up states: the per-hectare value already embeds it.

## Source

The write-up is `Non-Timber Forest Product Provision.docx` in the shared folder of current
write-ups (version of 29 October 2026). The registered author code is `Observarun/geo-ntfp` at
`928dc21`, a fork of `martaszk/geo_ntfp` that adds the NDVI screen. The library follows its rules
on the account's own grid.

## Quantity

Hectares of accessible, vegetated forest per country:

- Forest is ESA CCI 2019 land cover, classes 50 to 90 inclusive.
- A forest cell is kept where the 2015 to 2019 mean NDVI (MODIS MOD13Q1) is at least 0.20. A
  cell with no NDVI is dropped. The floor is compared in the raster's own integers, so a cell at
  exactly 0.20 is kept, where the authors' float comparison drops it.
- Accessible means within 10 km of a road (`globalroads.shp`) or a river (Natural Earth 10 m
  centre lines).
- Everything is computed on the account grid (WGS84, 10 arcsec, about 309 m at the equator), with
  the 10 km reach measured in metres at each latitude. The reach stops at 84 degrees. Cell
  hectares come from `ha_per_cell_10sec.tif`, and a cell belongs to the country whose boundary
  covers its centre.

## Price

The CWoN 2024 non-wood forest product value per hectare per country, in current USD, read at the
GEP base year from `nontimber_price_iucn_edited.csv`.

## Valuation

`ntfp_gep_by_country` filters the value series to the base year, joins it onto the accessible-area
table by country label, and multiplies:

$$
\text{NTFP GEP} = \text{accessible forest (ha)} \times \text{NWFP value (USD/ha)}
$$

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `ntfp` service: `ntfp_roads_vector_path`,
`ntfp_rivers_path` (with its source URL), `ntfp_ndvi_mean_path` and `ntfp_value_per_ha_path`
(with its source URL). The land cover is the `es_config.csv` row's `gep_lulc_input_path`,
`lulc/esa/lulc_esa_2019.tif`.

## Output

`accessible_forest` writes `accessible_forest_ha_by_country.csv`, and `gep_calculation` writes
`gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the r250 identifiers and
attributes, `accessible_forest_ha`, `nwfp_value_per_ha`, `ntfp_gep` and `year`.

The accessibility step reads five global rasters of 8.4 billion cells each, in blocks, and runs
on the cluster.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019
USD. 196 carry a positive value, totalling \$13,852,553,747.75 on 1.44 billion accessible
hectares. 36 are zeros, all measured: 34 have no accessible forest and 11 have a published zero
rate, 9 of them both. 18 are missing because the CWoN table has no rate for them (ATA, BLM, BVT,
CCK, ESH, HMD, IOT, KWT, MAF, MCO, MDV, MHL, MSR, NRU, PCN, TKL, TUV, VAT).

## Reproduction

Rate times saved hectares reproduces every published row, and the rate column equals the staged
table's 2019 column. The authors' own per-country output is not supplied. Against the ten
country values in the write-up's table, the library is 0.961 times their sum, from 0.838
(Russia) to 0.999 (Brazil). The shortfall concentrates at high latitude, consistent with the
authors' 10 km buffers drawn in Mollweide against the account grid's metric reach, though that is
not tested country by country. The account grid replaces the authors' Mollweide 300 m grid, which
gave \$14.07bn, so the change is −1.6%.

## Method constants

- `NTFP_ACCESS_BUFFER_M = 10_000`, the accessibility reach around roads and rivers.
- `ESA_FOREST_CLASS_MIN = 50` and `ESA_FOREST_CLASS_MAX = 90`, the inclusive forest class range.
- `NDVI_MIN_THRESHOLD = 0.20`, the vegetation floor.

## What is open

- The denominator. The source report averages the per-hectare value over a country's total
  forest and multiplies by total forest area, while the account applies it to accessible forest
  only. On 148 shared countries that area base accounts for −\$17.10bn of the gap to CWoN's
  total. The question is with Marta (open question 15).
- Three rates. The staged table's rates for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mozambique and
  the Central African Republic are five times CWoN's own, which divides them by five without a
  stated reason. Applying it gives \$12.76bn. A recorded open decision.
- The grid. The account grid is agreed (29 October), and its effect against the authors' grid
  is measured in total only.
